newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa tightly mixed at noon after new high.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa tightly mixed at noon after new high.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures pulled back to end Monday midsession tightly mixed after an early run-up which propelled benchmark September to a new one-year high, traders said.
But activity was dull and little trade was seen on either side of the market this morning. There was no spec or fund involvement.
Traders said the market was probably heading for a breather after last week's rally on heavy trade and fund buying.
"The market is resting a bit," said one, saying that the market was trying to build a base after the rally on Thursday and Friday.
"It needs something fresh to get it going again," he added.

September peaked at 1,140 stg per tonne, the highest on the second month since June 16, 1996 and a fresh contract high, before slipping back on trade profit-taking. It ended midsession down two stg at 1,126 stg.
Front-month July matched Friday's life-of-contract high at 1,122 stg before ending the morning business six stg down at 1,110.

Friday's rally extended Thursday's surge on concerns the developing El Nino weather pattern would spark droughts in major cocoa-producing countries and disrupt next year's cocoa crop. There was also talk that early Ivory Coast settings for the new crop remained low.

Though some traders were sceptical of the fundamental change said to be pushing cocoa prices higher, they said they could not ignore the strong uptrend developing on near- and intermediate-term technical charts.
Traders said there was also talk that a U.S. crop forecaster Hans Killian had released what some regarded as a fairly bullish Ivorian crop estimate.
